## Historical audit — S0293, chunk 1 of 2

**Source for all rows:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/selection/bw_0045/1/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and interpretation | The request was to reconstruct a 512 × 285 photograph as separate 3D meshes with matching camera and framing (H `model_request`, line 1). H’s inventory interpreted it as a dairy barn with reclining cows, stall dividers, a worker, wall and bedding; that interpretation is not independent inspection of the reference (H `model_response`, line 3). |
| Initial scene | H emitted seven cow assets, eight repeated divider assemblies, architecture, bedding and a worker. Cow child meshes included head, folded legs, udder and tail; rails included uprights and cross rails. Hierarchical inclusion is recorded, but physical part connection and reference fidelity are not verified. The code set colors, metallic/roughness values, a camera and two lights (H response line 3; `execute` step 1, line 4). |
| Validation and revision | Step 1 built and rendered successfully; `ok: true` and a saved image are recorded, followed by selection (lines 6–10). The next request supplied that image to H (line 11). H described the view as too wide and high, with disk-like markings, then executed a revised scene with a closer camera, extended surfaces and procedural hide; its code contains eight cows and ten dividers, despite comments estimating seven and nine (H response line 13; `execute` line 14). Step 2 also built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 16–20). |
| Further exploration | Given the second render, H reported a row receding toward the center, obscured or out-of-frame head and worker, overly fine hide and missing foreground aisle. It submitted and executed a third program changing camera side and coat scale and adding soiled rump geometry (H response line 23; `execute` line 24). The third build completed, and rendering started; its completion is not visible here (lines 26–27). These diagnoses are H’s observations, not independently verified image facts. |
| Teacher and autonomy | No teacher message, diagnosis or proposed update appears in this visible chunk; receipt or adoption cannot be established. H independently revised after runner-provided render feedback. The observed CLI sessions report no tool calls and disabled external exploration tools (lines 2, 12, 22); runner executions are separately recorded. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Two technical build/render successes are visible, not formal scene correctness. The third render, final selection and overall outcome are unknown in this chunk; no interruption or algorithm failure is established. Neither reference nor rendered pixels are visible to this audit, so object count in the photograph, pose, actual connections, texture quality, camera alignment, lighting and visual improvement remain unresolved. The third program retains lights, but no lighting defect or correction is independently established.

**Lessons.** Transferably, separating a render’s technical success from visual verification and comparing framing and local materials are useful audit distinctions. The claimed camera-side and hide-scale fixes are task-specific hypotheses; their effectiveness requires the unseen third render and comparison, not the code or asset names alone.
